outcome: On 6 October 2026 OpenAI posted, in its public openai/math GitHub repository, a manuscript titled 'A counterexample to Sidorenko's conjecture' that claims a bipartite graph on 35 vertices and 66 edges with a finite host graph violating the inequality; the repository's Lean statement of this is still marked sorry, no independent mathematician's check of the manuscript was found, and every other event since January 2024 is a partial result for a restricted class, a reduction, a negative computer search, or an analogue.
problem_asks: The statement, as frozen, is 'Sidorenko's conjecture on homomorphism densities of graphs in graphons'. Parts: (1) for every bipartite graph H, (2) and every graphon W with edge density p = t(K_2, W), the homomorphism density t(H, W) is at least p raised to the number of edges of H. The statement names no further parts; the universal quantifier over bipartite H is the only structure, so each bipartite H is one instance. Non-bipartite graphs are outside the claim. The frozen wording itself was not given beyond this title, so this unpacking is written from the title and the standard formulation.

events.what_happened: OpenAI released, in the public openai/math GitHub repository, a manuscript 'A counterexample to Sidorenko's conjecture' (folder name dated September 23, 2026; folder README: 'Author: OpenAI', 'Date: September 23, 2026'). The repository's first commit, 'Initial commit' by 'Anonymous', is dated 6 October 2026. The repository's CONTENTS.md entry 161, titled 'Counterexamples to Sidorenko's conjecture and the forcing conjecture', has the abstract 'Disproves Sidorenko's conjecture with a connected bipartite pattern on 35 vertices and 66 edges', and says the same pattern disproves 'the forcing conjecture of Skokan and Thoma'. The manuscript's own abstract line in CONTENTS reads 'We disprove Sidorenko's conjecture with a bipartite graph on 35 vertices and 66 edges.' The Wikipedia article's sentence 'On October 6th, 2026, OpenAI claimed a resolution of Sidorenko's Conjecture in the negative by providing a constructive counter example' links to the paper.pdf in that folder; the sentence was added by one editor on 7 October 2026 with no edit summary. The repo's Lean file lean/ComparatorChallenges/SidorenkoCounterexample.lean states 'theorem main : there exist size > 0 and a SimpleGraph host on Fin size with at least one edge and homDensity H host < (edgeDensity host) ^ 66', where H is a 35-vertex bipartite pattern (13 point vertices and 22 face vertices, adjacency = point lies in face); its proof body is 'sorry'. The paper PDF could not be read by me, so the host graph, the construction and the paper's own proof are not recorded here.
events.revisions: Initial commit 6 Oct 2026 (adc7f12). Commit 3014888 'Update manuscripts and Lean formalizations' dated 8 Oct 2026 (1,185 files changed; the Sidorenko Lean file and folder are not in the visible part of the file list, so what changed in them is unknown). history.md has one dated entry, 7 Oct 2026: three other manuscripts withdrawn (Weil classes on split abelian eightfolds, Kuga-Satake correspondences for K3 surfaces, rational Hodge conjecture for products of K3 surfaces), 14 revised; none is the Sidorenko manuscript. The folder's September 23 date appears only in the folder name and README; the earliest public posting I can date is 6 October.
events.delivers: If the manuscript and the Lean statement are right: one explicit bipartite pattern H with 35 vertices and 66 edges, and a finite simple host graph G with at least one edge, such that t(H, G) < t(K_2, G)^66. In the Lean statement homDensity counts all edge-preserving maps, including non-injective ones, normalised by N^|V(H)|, and edgeDensity is 2|E|/N^2, so these are the densities of the step graphon of G; the finite-host statement therefore transfers to the graphon formulation of the bullet. The claim is about one graph H, so it settles the universal claim 'every bipartite H is Sidorenko' negatively if it holds, and says nothing about any other bipartite graph. The repo's abstract also claims the same pattern disproves the forcing conjecture of Skokan and Thoma; the docs say that consequence is outside the Lean statement. The Lean file as read does not prove even the single-H statement (see doubts).
events.remains: Per the claim, the universal statement is refuted for this H, so no part of the bullet's universal claim is left open for this H. Not established by any file I could read: the existence of the host graph (the Lean statement is existential and carries sorry), the paper's proof, and the status of every other bipartite graph. The forcing-conjecture consequence is a different problem and is not part of this bullet.
events.time_since_posted: about one week as of 13 October 2026
events.directly_checkable: The pattern H is explicit in the Lean file: 13 point vertices and 22 face triples, with an edge when the point lies in the triple (22 x 3 = 66 incidences, which matches the stated edge count). Checking the inequality needs the host graph, which the Lean file does not name and the paper, which I could not read, presumably does. A reader with the paper can compute t(H, G) and t(K_2, G)^66 for the host by direct counting.
events.doubts: (a) The Lean theorem main ends in 'sorry' on main (fetched raw, c. 13 Oct 2026) and the same file at the initial commit adc7f12 also ends in 'sorry'. (b) The docs page lean/docs/161.md at adc7f12 says 'The formalization disproves this for the paper's fixed bipartite graph with 35 vertices and 66 edges', which the Lean file does not support; this is a conflict inside the repo, recorded in disputes. (c) The repo README says most results come from one internal-model procedure and that 'Some of the unformalized results could have issues'; the Sidorenko manuscript's Lean status is unknown. (d) No human reading of the manuscript was found in 38 searches. Coverage by Kalai (blog, 7 Oct 2026) describes the counterexample without a verification status; Nature (via aggregator) and Scientific American report expert scepticism about the batch generally (Sutherland: expect some proofs to contain mistakes) but not about this manuscript. (e) One secondary news source (news.lavx.hu, 7 Oct 2026) says none of the batch appears on arXiv under the same titles as of publication; I did not verify this. (f) Date discrepancy: the Wikipedia claim is dated 6 October, the folder and BibTeX label say 23 September. (g) Wikipedia's 'constructive' wording against the Lean statement, which is existential. (h) The Wikipedia article still says 'there are graphs for which Sidorenko's conjecture is still open' in the same article that reports the claim (see disputes).
events.direction: Against the conjecture as stated: it asserts that a specific bipartite graph H fails the Sidorenko inequality for some finite host graph, which contradicts the universal claim that every bipartite graph has the property.
events.object: A bipartite graph H on 35 vertices with 66 edges: 13 point vertices and 22 face vertices, where each face is a triple of points (the faces are Table 1 of the source; the Lean list begins {0,1,3}, {0,1,9}, {0,2,3}, ...), and a point is adjacent to a face when it lies in that triple. Claimed: a finite simple host graph G with at least one edge and t(H,G) < t(K_2,G)^66. Wikipedia calls the counterexample constructive; the Lean statement is existential and does not name G. Whether the paper gives an explicit G or a non-constructive argument is not recorded because I could not read the paper.

events.what_happened: Im, Li and Liu, 'Sidorenko's conjecture for subdivisions and theta substitutions' (arXiv:2408.03491). Replacing each edge of a graph H by a generalised theta graph (even paths joining the same two ends) gives a graph with the Sidorenko property provided a divisibility condition on the number of paths holds; unconditionally, for bipartite graphs obtained by replacing each edge of a complete graph by a generalised theta graph (extending Conlon, Kim, Lee and Lee 2018). Later listed in Combinatorics, Probability and Computing 35 (2026) 269-279 (Cambridge Core listing from search, not opened).
events.delivers: Sidorenko's inequality for a restricted family: bipartite graphs made from a complete graph by replacing each edge with a generalised theta graph (unconditional), and a conditional version for general H with a divisibility condition on path counts.
events.remains: Every bipartite graph outside these families, including the general conjecture, and the conditional case where the divisibility fails.

checked_by.qualification: Journal of record; acceptance follows referee review
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper in volume 35 (2026), pp. 269-279, per a Cambridge Core listing that appeared in search (not opened by me)

events.direction: Positive, for restricted families only.

events.what_happened: Kiem, Parczyk and Spiegel, arXiv:2412.12904. Establish Sidorenko and forcing-conjecture results for balanced blow-ups of Sidorenko graphs, subdivisions of Sidorenko graphs by a forcing graph, and Cartesian and strong products, via an adjoint identity for graph-substitution operators. Version 2 (21 Sep 2026) is a 'completely rewritten version' with substantially revised proofs.
events.revisions: v1 17 Dec 2024; v2 21 Sep 2026, 'completely rewritten version of the original submission'.
events.delivers: Sidorenko property (and forcing) for the named constructions applied to Sidorenko graphs and forcing graphs. Restricted to those operations.
events.remains: The general conjecture, and every bipartite graph not produced by these constructions from known Sidorenko or forcing graphs.
events.direction: Positive, for restricted constructions only.

events.what_happened: Zhao, 'Sidorenko-Type Inequalities for Even Subdivisions over Finite Abelian Groups' (arXiv:2507.15723). Proves Sidorenko's conjecture for all even subdivisions of arbitrary graphs when the host is a Cayley graph over a finite abelian group, using Fourier analysis on solution sets of linear systems over finite abelian groups; cites Szegedy's reduction of the conjecture to Cayley hosts over finite groups.
events.delivers: Sidorenko property for the class of even subdivisions (each edge replaced by a path of even length), with host graphs restricted to Cayley graphs over finite abelian groups.
events.remains: General host graphs (Szegedy's reduction leaves Cayley hosts over arbitrary finite groups, including non-abelian ones), and all bipartite graphs outside the even-subdivision class.
events.direction: Positive, for a restricted class and restricted hosts.

events.what_happened: Georgiev, Gomez-Serrano, Tao and Wagner, 'Mathematical exploration and discovery at scale' (arXiv:2511.02864), section on Sidorenko's conjecture (section 6.11 in the table of contents I read). They used AlphaEvolve to search for a graphon W violating the Sidorenko inequality for H = K_{5,5} minus a 10-cycle, the smallest bipartite graph not known to be Sidorenko, with a penalty against near-constant graphons. Conclusion: 'we did not manage to find a counterexample to this conjecture.' Terence Tao blogged the paper on 5 November 2025 and quoted the outcome for the search: AlphaEvolve 'did not locate any stronger counterexamples: thus, we did not disprove any major open conjecture.'

events.remains: Everything; the search found no counterexample and proved no inequality.

events.what_happened: Li, Lin, Liu and Zhang, 'Spectral Sidorenko inequalities and edge-spectral supersaturation' (arXiv:2605.26614). Shows that Sidorenko's conjecture for bipartite H with v(H) at most e(H) is equivalent to a spectral strengthening; gives operator-norm certificates with direct proofs of the spectral inequality in several unnamed cases; proves supersaturation bounds for K_{t,t} and C_{2t} for degenerate bipartite graphs that already have the Sidorenko property.
events.delivers: An equivalence between the conjecture and a spectral form for the stated class of H; no graph is shown to be Sidorenko in full generality by this result, and the supersaturation results assume the Sidorenko property.
events.remains: The conjecture itself for every bipartite graph; the spectral inequality for the general class.
events.direction: Reduction, neither way on the conjecture itself.

events.what_happened: Zhao, 'Conjugacy Class Averages and Sidorenko's Conjecture' (arXiv:2606.15368). Gives a reduction: if for every finite group and every nonnegative weight the Cayley-type host has H-density at least that of its conjugacy-class average, then H is strong Sidorenko and hence Sidorenko. Also proves a Sidorenko-type inequality for 1-subdivision graphs on conjugacy-averaged Cayley kernels.
events.delivers: Conditional: the reduction applies to a bipartite H once a density comparison is verified for every Cayley-type host, which the abstract does not establish for any specific H. Unconditional but narrow: a Sidorenko-type inequality for 1-subdivisions on conjugacy-averaged Cayley kernels.
events.remains: The general conjecture; the density comparison for every host; all bipartite H outside 1-subdivisions.
events.direction: Reduction and partial result; neither way on the conjecture itself.

events.what_happened: Zhao, 'Tensor Amplification and Spectral Transfer for Sidorenko-Type Inequalities' (arXiv:2607.02260). A framework for Sidorenko-type inequalities on graphon classes closed under tensor powers and normalised principal restrictions; proves equality regularisation for non-matching C-Sidorenko graphs and a spectral equivalence for graphs with v(H) at most e(H), within admissible classes. Applies to doubly nonnegative graphons.
events.delivers: Equivalences and regularity within stated admissible graphon classes; the abstract does not claim the general conjecture and does not identify a newly covered bipartite graph for the unrestricted problem.
events.remains: The conjecture for general graphons and for all bipartite graphs.
events.direction: Equivalence within classes; neither way on the conjecture itself.

events.what_happened: Zhao, 'Sidorenko Inequalities for Two-Sided Group Correlation Kernels' (arXiv:2606.23018). Proves a Sidorenko-type lower bound for every finite directed graph F in a two-sided correlation kernel on a finite group, with a directed 1-subdivision variant. Directed graphs and group kernels, not undirected graphon densities.
events.delivers: A different question: directed graphs in group correlation kernels. It does not address the undirected graphon statement in this bullet.
events.remains: The undirected conjecture for graphs and graphons, entirely.
events.direction: Analogue; does not bear on the undirected statement.

events.what_happened: The manuscript 'A counterexample to Sidorenko's conjecture' (OpenAI, dated September 23, 2026) is the only manuscript in this family. It claims one bipartite graph H on 35 vertices and 66 edges, and a finite simple graph G with at least one edge, such that t(H,G) < p(G)⁶⁶. Here t(H,G) is the homomorphism density (non-injective maps counted, normalised by |V(G)|^|V(H)|) and p(G) = 2|E(G)|/|V(G)|² is the edge density. H is the incidence graph of 22 triples on 13 points, listed explicitly in Table 'tab:complex' (sections/complex.tex); it is connected, with parts of size 13 and 22, degrees 4, 5 and 6 on the point side and 3 on the face side. The argument has three steps. (1) A finite symmetric [0,1]-valued kernel U with mean μ > 0 and t(H,U) < μ⁶⁶ is built from a rectangular kernel over random symmetric matrices over F_q, symmetrised by a crossed product and diluted (Proposition 'negative-kernel', sections/kernel.tex). (2) That step is conditional on the rank-layer limit, Lemma 'Rank-layer limit', which the manuscript proves in its own Sections 3 to 6. (3) A finite simple host G on n vertices is sampled from U, with n > (595 + 66μ⁶⁶)/Δ and Δ = μ⁶⁶ − t(H,U) (Lemma 'finite-host'). The same manuscript also refutes the graphon form: the {0,1} adjacency kernel W₀ of G on the uniform measure on V(G) has t(K₂,W₀) = p(G) and t(H,W₀) = t(H,G) < p(G)⁶⁶ (proof of Corollary 'Failure of the forcing conjecture', sections/consequences.tex). The manuscript also claims, for this same H, a failure of the Conlon–Fox–Sudakov forcing conjecture and amplification and injective-copy results. Those are not matched problems here and are not described further.
events.delivers: Disproves Sidorenko's conjecture as the list states it. The conjecture quantifies over every bipartite graph H, so a single bipartite H with t(H,W) < t(K₂,W)^{e(H)} for some graphon W refutes the universal claim. The counterexample is for this one graph, which is connected, bipartite and has 35 vertices and 66 edges. It is given in the finite-graph form (a finite simple host G with at least one edge). The graphon form in the list is also refuted, by the step graphon W₀ of G, since t(K₂,W₀) = p(G) and t(H,W₀) = t(H,G). The manuscript's own statement (its displayed inequality, with p(G) = 2|E|/|V|² for finite simple G, and 'bipartite with at least one edge') matches the list's statement up to the finite-graph versus graphon wording, which W₀ bridges. The manuscript says 'We disprove this conjecture', so it claims a full negative answer to the universal statement, not a partial or sharpened one. The manuscript also notes that H has no vertex adjacent to the whole opposite part, is not weakly norming (its point-side degrees are not regular), and fails the degree-count hypotheses of the positive results it cites. So it does not contradict those positive theorems, which concern other graphs.
events.remains: If the claim is correct, the universal statement as frozen is false and nothing of it remains open. Not addressed: which bipartite graphs do satisfy the inequality, beyond the positive classes already known; whether H is minimal in size or edge count; and whether any local or restricted version holds for H (the manuscript says the local kernel results of Lovász do not apply to its kernel). The host G is given only by existence, not explicitly.

machine_checked.scope: Sidorenko's conjecture predicts that every bipartite graph $H$ has homomorphism density at least the host graph's edge density raised to $|E(H)|$. The formalization disproves this for the paper's fixed bipartite graph with $35$ vertices and $66$ edges: it constructs a nonempty finite simple host graph with $t(H,G)<t(K_2,G)^{66}$. The separate forcing-conjecture consequence in the paper is outside this statement.

events.doubts: (1) The rank-layer lemma carries the whole result. Its proof spans about 2,400 lines (Sections 3 to 6). I read its statement, the assembly at the end of tail.tex, and the passages flagged here, not the full proof. (2) The singular-contribution proposition (tail.tex, 'Vanishing singular contribution') bounds the local maximising tuples only by necessary dimension inequalities. The text says these 'need not be realizable simultaneously', so the bound is an upper bound by design. (3) The numerical remainder 1641 and the requirement D > 1641 (tail.tex, 'Costs for the remaining profiles' and the singular-contribution proof) are asserted. The text says D > 1641 'is needed here only for the nondirect residual case and is not asserted to be a threshold for the whole proof'. I did not check the derivation of 1641. (4) The choice of D, ε and q is non-quantitative throughout, so the existence of G is not quantified. (5) In the rank-layer proof, the comparison that drops the prescribed signs off the transverse set is dismissed in one sentence: 'dropping the prescribed signs only enlarges the integrand after the comparable normalizations'. (6) The finite-host proof calls the probability that a map is a homomorphism a 'homomorphism indicator between zero and one'. The quantity is a probability; the collision bound is unaffected. (7) The abstract, the displayed theorem and the corollary statements agree on 35 vertices, 66 edges and a strict inequality for a finite simple graph with at least one edge.; conditional on: No external unproven hypothesis is stated for the Sidorenko disproof. Internally, the finite kernel (Proposition 'negative-kernel') and the host lemma are proved conditional on Lemma 'Rank-layer limit' (kernel.tex). The manuscript proves that lemma itself in Sections 3 to 6 (transverse, orbits, planted, tail), so the dependence is internal rather than on another paper. The sampling step follows the standard graphon sampling construction of Lovász and Szegedy (Section 2.6, Lemma 2.4) and gives its own collision bound. Standard inputs used without re-proof are the quadratic Gauss-sum rank bound (Gowers–Wolf, Lemma 3.3), the association-scheme counts of symmetric matrices by rank and sign (Huo–Wan; Schmidt), the Lagrangian counting formulas (Taylor), and the colour-refinement facts (Weisfeiler–Leman; McKay).
events.direction: disproves the conjecture (one bipartite graph on 35 vertices and 66 edges)
events.object: H is explicit: the incidence graph of 22 triples on 13 points, all triples written out in Table 'tab:complex' (sections/complex.tex). The host G is not explicit. It is produced by a probabilistic sampling argument from a finite kernel, after choosing a large fixed even dimension D, a small ε > 0 and a large odd prime q, each chosen only as 'sufficiently large' or 'sufficiently small'. The manuscript does not write G down and does not give its order beyond the existential bound n > (595 + 66μ⁶⁶)/Δ, where Δ depends on the constructed kernel.

disputes.summary: The OpenAI repo's docs page lean/docs/161.md (at commit adc7f12, 6 Oct 2026) says the formalization 'disproves' the conjecture for the 35-vertex, 66-edge pattern. The Lean file lean/ComparatorChallenges/SidorenkoCounterexample.lean, both at adc7f12 and on main as I read it, states theorem main with proof 'sorry'. The docs claim is not supported by the file; I did not verify whether the file changed in commit 3014888 (8 Oct 2026), whose diff I could not inspect.

The Wikipedia article reports the OpenAI claim in the negative, but its status text still says there are graphs for which the conjecture is still open (naming the K_{5,5} minus C_{10} 'Mobius strip' graph). The claim's sentence was added 7 Oct 2026 by one editor; another edit on 8 Oct 2026 deduplicated a reference. Whether the article's 'still open' sentence is stale or still correct is not settled by the sources I read; K_{5,5} minus C_{10} has 10 vertices, while the claimed H has 35.

summary: Found one in-window claim that would settle the bullet negatively, and a set of partial results. The claim: on 6 October 2026, the public openai/math repository (first commit dated 6 October 2026) posted a manuscript, 'A counterexample to Sidorenko's conjecture', whose folder is dated 23 September 2026 and whose author line reads 'OpenAI'. The repository's catalogue entry 161 (CONTENTS.md, raw fetch) says it disproves the conjecture with a bipartite graph on 35 vertices and 66 edges, and that the same pattern disproves the Skokan-Thoma forcing conjecture. Wikipedia's Sidorenko article reports 'a claimed resolution ... in the negative by providing a constructive counter example', linking the paper; that sentence was added on 7 October 2026. The Lean file for the counterexample states the existence of a finite host graph with homDensity below edgeDensity^66 for the 35-vertex pattern, but its proof is 'sorry' on main and at the initial commit, while the repo's docs page says the formalization disproves the conjecture; I record this as a formalization-status dispute. I could not read the paper PDF: WebFetch returns undecodable binary, and a stdin text-extraction pipeline needed Bash approval that was not granted, so the host graph, the construction, and the paper's own AI declaration are unrecorded. Independent checking: none found. Kalai's blog (7 Oct 2026) describes the counterexample without a verification status; batch-level coverage (Scientific American, Retraction Watch, a Nature aggregator) reports scepticism about the batch and three withdrawn manuscripts, none on Sidorenko. Two near-identical GitHub repositories build on the construction (a 35-vertex minimum within a finite template with exact certificates; described as written with Codex) and disclaim priority and formal verification. AI: the repo README attributes the manuscripts, including this one as far as it goes, to 'an internal OpenAI model' (unreleased), with about three hours of ChatGPT Pro compute per result on average; the Sidorenko manuscript is not among the README's named exceptions. That is repository-level, not paper-specific. Partial results in window: Im-Li-Liu (Aug 2024, restricted families, refereed in CPC), Kiem-Parczyk-Spiegel (Dec 2024, constructions), Zhao (Jul 2025, even subdivisions with abelian Cayley hosts), Li-Lin-Liu-Zhang (May 2026, spectral equivalence), Zhao (Jun 2026, conditional reduction plus a 1-subdivision result), Zhao (Jul 2026, framework within admissible classes). Negative AI searches: AlphaEvolve on K_{5,5} minus C_{10} (Nov 2025; Tao blog confirms no counterexample) and a Duke Math+ RL/AMCS project (2025). Analogues discarded: tournament and hypergraph papers (2025-2026) and a different star inequality (Luchtrath-Monch, 2024). Pre-window: Conlon-Lee-Sidorenko (2023), Li-Szegedy (2011), Garg-Raymond-Redlich (2022), Blekherman et al. (2018). Close call: whether a claimed 35-vertex counterexample with an explicit Lean-style statement, but with a sorry, no visible independent check, and a paper I could not read, counts as 'resolved' or as 'claimed' is for the judging pass; I record it as claimed and unverified. Where the sources disagree, the disagreement is recorded in disputes.
competing_reading: The claim could be read as settled negatively already: the bullet asks whether every bipartite graph is Sidorenko, one valid finite counterexample refutes it, the pattern is explicit (13 points, 22 triples, 66 incidences), the Lean statement is a simple existential whose truth could be checked by computing one host, OpenAI's batch has shown some errors being caught and withdrawn, and the repo's own docs say the formalization disproves the conjecture. Against that reading: the repo's Lean file proves nothing (sorry), no host graph is named in any file I could read, the paper was unreadable to me, no mathematician has been found checking the Sidorenko manuscript, and the batch README itself warns that unformalised results 'could have issues'.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The paper PDF's text: the host graph, the density computation, and the paper's AI declaration. (2) A Lean build of theorem main with no sorry, or the Comparator result for SidorenkoCounterexample.lean, with the commit in which it changed. (3) A named expert's public check of the host graph's density (computed by hand or by a verified script) or a written review. (4) The commit diff of 3014888 for the Sidorenko Lean file and folder. (5) An arXiv or journal version, or a withdrawal.

event.what_happened: OpenAI released, in the public openai/math GitHub repository, a manuscript 'A counterexample to Sidorenko's conjecture' (folder name dated September 23, 2026; folder README: 'Author: OpenAI', 'Date: September 23, 2026'). The repository's first commit, 'Initial commit' by 'Anonymous', is dated 6 October 2026. The repository's CONTENTS.md entry 161, titled 'Counterexamples to Sidorenko's conjecture and the forcing conjecture', has the abstract 'Disproves Sidorenko's conjecture with a connected bipartite pattern on 35 vertices and 66 edges', and says the same pattern disproves 'the forcing conjecture of Skokan and Thoma'. The manuscript's own abstract line in CONTENTS reads 'We disprove Sidorenko's conjecture with a bipartite graph on 35 vertices and 66 edges.' The Wikipedia article's sentence 'On October 6th, 2026, OpenAI claimed a resolution of Sidorenko's Conjecture in the negative by providing a constructive counter example' links to the paper.pdf in that folder; the sentence was added by one editor on 7 October 2026 with no edit summary. The repo's Lean file lean/ComparatorChallenges/SidorenkoCounterexample.lean states 'theorem main : there exist size > 0 and a SimpleGraph host on Fin size with at least one edge and homDensity H host < (edgeDensity host) ^ 66', where H is a 35-vertex bipartite pattern (13 point vertices and 22 face vertices, adjacency = point lies in face); its proof body is 'sorry'. The paper PDF could not be read by me, so the host graph, the construction and the paper's own proof are not recorded here.
event.revisions: Initial commit 6 Oct 2026 (adc7f12). Commit 3014888 'Update manuscripts and Lean formalizations' dated 8 Oct 2026 (1,185 files changed; the Sidorenko Lean file and folder are not in the visible part of the file list, so what changed in them is unknown). history.md has one dated entry, 7 Oct 2026: three other manuscripts withdrawn (Weil classes on split abelian eightfolds, Kuga-Satake correspondences for K3 surfaces, rational Hodge conjecture for products of K3 surfaces), 14 revised; none is the Sidorenko manuscript. The folder's September 23 date appears only in the folder name and README; the earliest public posting I can date is 6 October.
event.delivers: If the manuscript and the Lean statement are right: one explicit bipartite pattern H with 35 vertices and 66 edges, and a finite simple host graph G with at least one edge, such that t(H, G) < t(K_2, G)^66. In the Lean statement homDensity counts all edge-preserving maps, including non-injective ones, normalised by N^|V(H)|, and edgeDensity is 2|E|/N^2, so these are the densities of the step graphon of G; the finite-host statement therefore transfers to the graphon formulation of the bullet. The claim is about one graph H, so it settles the universal claim 'every bipartite H is Sidorenko' negatively if it holds, and says nothing about any other bipartite graph. The repo's abstract also claims the same pattern disproves the forcing conjecture of Skokan and Thoma; the docs say that consequence is outside the Lean statement. The Lean file as read does not prove even the single-H statement (see doubts).
event.remains: Per the claim, the universal statement is refuted for this H, so no part of the bullet's universal claim is left open for this H. Not established by any file I could read: the existence of the host graph (the Lean statement is existential and carries sorry), the paper's proof, and the status of every other bipartite graph. The forcing-conjecture consequence is a different problem and is not part of this bullet.
event.time_since_posted: about one week as of 13 October 2026
event.directly_checkable: The pattern H is explicit in the Lean file: 13 point vertices and 22 face triples, with an edge when the point lies in the triple (22 x 3 = 66 incidences, which matches the stated edge count). Checking the inequality needs the host graph, which the Lean file does not name and the paper, which I could not read, presumably does. A reader with the paper can compute t(H, G) and t(K_2, G)^66 for the host by direct counting.
event.doubts: (a) The Lean theorem main ends in 'sorry' on main (fetched raw, c. 13 Oct 2026) and the same file at the initial commit adc7f12 also ends in 'sorry'. (b) The docs page lean/docs/161.md at adc7f12 says 'The formalization disproves this for the paper's fixed bipartite graph with 35 vertices and 66 edges', which the Lean file does not support; this is a conflict inside the repo, recorded in disputes. (c) The repo README says most results come from one internal-model procedure and that 'Some of the unformalized results could have issues'; the Sidorenko manuscript's Lean status is unknown. (d) No human reading of the manuscript was found in 38 searches. Coverage by Kalai (blog, 7 Oct 2026) describes the counterexample without a verification status; Nature (via aggregator) and Scientific American report expert scepticism about the batch generally (Sutherland: expect some proofs to contain mistakes) but not about this manuscript. (e) One secondary news source (news.lavx.hu, 7 Oct 2026) says none of the batch appears on arXiv under the same titles as of publication; I did not verify this. (f) Date discrepancy: the Wikipedia claim is dated 6 October, the folder and BibTeX label say 23 September. (g) Wikipedia's 'constructive' wording against the Lean statement, which is existential. (h) The Wikipedia article still says 'there are graphs for which Sidorenko's conjecture is still open' in the same article that reports the claim (see disputes).
event.direction: Against the conjecture as stated: it asserts that a specific bipartite graph H fails the Sidorenko inequality for some finite host graph, which contradicts the universal claim that every bipartite graph has the property.
event.object: A bipartite graph H on 35 vertices with 66 edges: 13 point vertices and 22 face vertices, where each face is a triple of points (the faces are Table 1 of the source; the Lean list begins {0,1,3}, {0,1,9}, {0,2,3}, ...), and a point is adjacent to a face when it lies in that triple. Claimed: a finite simple host graph G with at least one edge and t(H,G) < t(K_2,G)^66. Wikipedia calls the counterexample constructive; the Lean statement is existential and does not name G. Whether the paper gives an explicit G or a non-constructive argument is not recorded because I could not read the paper.

judgement.why: The statement is a single universal claim over bipartite H, so one valid bipartite counterexample answers it in full: both OpenAI rows (which describe the same manuscript, once from the repo surface and once from its LaTeX source) are scope whole, direction refuted, object counterexample (H explicit, host G existential via sampling). Neither is digested: no named human has read it, the Lean theorem carries sorry, and a docs page claiming formal disproof is not verification (F7); the object is not directly checkable since G is never written down. Doubtful rather than not_credible: a serious, detailed argument with no identified error, but disputed formal status and an AI batch with known withdrawals. AI role is generated from the README, which attributes the manuscripts to the internal model and does not list this one as an exception. Im-Li-Liu and Kiem-Parczyk-Spiegel prove the full inequality for restricted classes of H (case); Im-Li-Liu is counted digested on the CPC publication. Zhao's even-subdivision result restricts the hosts to abelian Cayley graphs, which proves a weaker statement for those H, so variant. Reductions, equivalences, method barriers and negative searches are none; tournament, hypergraph, directed and star-inequality papers are variants. The 2025 and 2026 year-only dates are both unambiguously after January 2024.
judgement.doubts: The two OpenAI events duplicate one manuscript; answered identically. AI credit for the manuscript rests on a repository-level README, not a paper-specific declaration. Im-Li-Liu's journal publication was seen only in a search listing. Codex role in the follow-up repositories is stated only as 'AI-generated draft'; immaterial since scope is none.
